source.text: ወእምድኅረዝ፡ ነስሐ፡ ርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡ ወይቤ፡ በከን፡ አሐጐልክዎሙ፡ ለኵሎሙ፡ ለእለ፡ ይነብሩ፡ ውስተ፡ የብስ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: After this the Head of Days regretted it and said, “In vain I destroyed all those who dwell on dry land.”

footnotes.text: The source says that the Head of Days regretted it and calls the destruction in vain. That wording is retained rather than softened to a different action. Head of Days is the printed title; no personal identification is supplied.

source.text: ወመሐለ፡ በስሙ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ከመ፡ እምይእዜ፡ ኢይገብር፡ ከመዝ፡ ለኵሎሙ፡ እለ፡ ይነብሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ፡ ወትእምርተ፡ አውዲ፡ በሰማያት፡ ወይከውን፡ ማእከለየ፡ ወ*ማእከሌሆሙ፡ ነይመወት፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም፡ መጠነ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሰማይ፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወ*ዝ፡ በትእዛዝየ፡ ውእቱ።]......
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used. HOLD: The word provisionally represented as ነይመወት immediately before እስከ is not glyph-certified; do not publish or substitute familiar English wording.

translation.text: He swore by his great name that from now on he would not do this to all who dwell on dry land: “I will set a sign in the heavens, and it will be between me and them [word not yet resolved] for ever, as long as heaven is above earth. This is by my command.”

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: the word between between-me-and-them and until/for-ever is not yet glyph-certified. The English marks that unresolved word instead of replacing it from a familiar English edition. The source also ends this unit with a closing editorial bracket and six dots; no missing text has been invented. The text moves from third-person swearing and not-doing into first-person speech.

source.text: ሶበ፡ ፈቂድኩ፡ ከመ፡ እዐግቶሙ፡ በእደ፡ መላእክት፡ በዕለተ፡ ምንዳቤ፡ ወሐማም፡ ቅድመዝ፡ *መቅሠፍትየ፡ ወመዐትየ፡ *እኀድር፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ ይቤ፡ እግዚአብሔር፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: “When I choose to surround them by the hand of the angels on the day of distress and pain, I will first cause my chastisement and my anger to settle upon them,” says God, the Lord of Spirits.

footnotes.text: The opening word is when, not a first-person pronoun. Surround follows the selected restraining or encircling verb. The source places my chastisement and my anger before the causative settle/dwell verb; first renders before this without adding an unprinted date or a new punishment.

source.text: ነገሥት፡ ኀያላን፡ እለ፡ ትኀድሩ፡ የብስ፡ ትርእይዎ፡ ሀለወክሙ፡ ለኅሩየ፡ ዚአየ፡ ከመ፡ ይነብር፡ ውስተ፡ መንበረ፡ ስብሐት፡ ወይኰንኖ፡ ለአዛዝኤል፡ ወለኵሎሙ፡ ማኅበረ፡ ዚአሁ፡ *ወለትዕይንተ፡ ዚአሁ፡ እለ፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used. HOLD: The final relative clause እለ፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት is syntactically awkward as selected. Do not silently discard እለ to turn in-the-name into an unambiguous adverbial of judging.

translation.text: You kings and mighty ones who dwell on dry land must see my chosen one as he sits on the throne of glory and judges Azazel and all his company and his troops, those who are in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: the selected final clause includes the relative word those who and then in the name of the Lord of Spirits, without an explicit predicate. The provisional English leaves that awkwardness visible. It does not silently drop the relative word or certify whether in the name modifies judging or the troops. The selected text calls the chosen one my chosen one and names Azazel.

source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ በህየ፡ ትዕይንተ፡ መላእክተ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ እንዘ፡ የሐውሩ፡ ወይኤኅዙ፡ *መቅሠፍተ፡ ወመሠጋግረ፡ ሐፂን፡ ወብርት።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: There I saw troops of angels of punishment going, holding scourges and fetters of iron and bronze.

footnotes.text: The selected word for the first object is scourges or instruments of punishment, not the distinct word rendered fetters. The metals are iron and bronze or copper; bronze does not assert a modern alloy specification. Troops renders the printed collective rather than an added numerical count.

source.text: ወተስእልክዎ፡ ለመልአኩ፡ ሰላም፡ ዘየሐውር፡ ምስሌየ፡ *እንዘ፡ እብል፡ ለመኑ፡ የሐውሩ፡ *እሉ፡ እለ፡ ይኤኅዙ፡ መቅሠፍተ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: I asked the angel of peace who was going with me, “To whom are these going, these who hold the scourges?”

footnotes.text: The question is to whom the bearers of the scourges are going. Angel of peace and the first-person companion relationship are retained; the text does not add the angel’s personal name.

source.text: ወይቤለኒ፡ ለኅሩያነ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ወለፍቁራኒሆሙ፡ ከመ፡ ይትወደዩ፡ ውስተ፡ ንቅዐተ፡ ማዕምቀ፡ ዝቈላ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: He said to me, “To their chosen and beloved ones, so that they may be thrown into the deep clefts of this valley.”

footnotes.text: The possessive their belongs to both chosen and beloved ones in the selected text. It is not changed to God’s chosen ones, and the antecedent is not supplied as an additional named group. Deep clefts renders the fissure and depth nouns; the final valley is not turned into an unprinted furnace.

source.text: ወእምዝ፡ ይመልእ፡ ውእቱ፡ ቈላ፡ እምነ፡ ኅሩያን፡ ወ*ፍቁራነ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ወይትዌዳእ፡ ዕለተ፡ ሕይወቶሙ፡ ወዕለተ፡ ስሕተቶሙ፡ እምይእዜ፡ ኢትትኄለቍ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: Then that valley will be filled with their chosen and beloved ones. Their days of life will come to an end, and from then on the days of their wrongdoing will not be counted.

footnotes.text: The selected negative belongs to the counting of the days of their wrongdoing: those days will no longer be counted. It is not moved backward to make the days of life innumerable. Their chosen and beloved ones retains the same possessive as the preceding unit.

source.text: ወበእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ይትጋብኡ፡ መላእክት፡ ወይመይጡ፡ እርእስቲሆሙ፡ *ለምሥራቅ፡ ላዕለ፡ ሰብአ፡ ጳርት፡ ወመዴ፡ የሐውስዎሙ፡ ለነገሥት፡ ወ*ያረውኡ፡ ልበሎሙ፡ መንፈሰ፡ ሁከት፡ ወ*ይሌውእዎሙ፡ እምመናብሪሆሙ፡ ወይወፅኡ፡ ከመ፡ አናብስት፡ እምምስካባቲሆሙ፡ ወከመ፡ አዛእብት፡ ርኁባን፡ ማእከለ፡ መርዔት፡ ዚአሆሙ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: In those days the angels will gather and turn their heads eastward, toward the people of Parthia and Media. They will stir up the kings and rouse a spirit of turmoil in their hearts, and they will remove them from their thrones. They will go out like lions from their lairs, like hungry wolves in the midst of their pasture.

footnotes.text: The selected verb says the angels gather. The names are the people of Parthia and Media, not a general reference to Persia. No modern country, campaign, or date is inserted. The complete unit continues onto the next page through both the lion and hungry-wolf comparisons.

source.text: ወ*ይዐርጉ፡ ወ*ይከይዱ፡ ላዕለ፡ ኅሩየ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ወትከውን፡ ምድረ፡ ኅሩያነ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ለ*ቅድሜሆሙ፡ ምክያደ፡ ወአሰረ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: They will go up and march against his chosen one. The land of his chosen ones will become a threshing floor and a track before them.

footnotes.text: The selected first clause has the singular his chosen one; the next clause has the plural his chosen ones. That distinction is retained. Threshing floor and track follow the two selected nouns; the first clause is not silently rewritten as trampling the land.

source.text: ወሀገረ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ዚአየ፡ ይከውን፡ ማዕቀፈ፡ ለአፍራሲሆሙ፡ ወያነሥእ፡ በበ፡ በይናቲሆሙ፡ ቀትለ፡ ወትጸንዕ፡ የማኖሙ፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ ወኢየአምር፡ ብእሲ፡ ለእኁሁ፡ ወኢወልድ፡ *ለአቡሁ፡ ወለእሙ፡ እስከ፡ ይከውን፡ ኁልቆ፡ አስከሬንት፡ †እሞቶሙ፡ ወመቅሠፍቶሙ፡ ኢትኩን፡ በከ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used. HOLD: Printed dagger on the from-their-death phrase; selected syntax does not straightforwardly justify an innumerable-corpses reading. No unprinted negative or retroverted Hebrew emendation adopted.

translation.text: The city of my righteous ones will be an obstacle to their horses. It will stir up killing among them, and their right hand will prevail against themselves. A man will not recognize his brother, nor a son his father or mother, until there is a count of corpses from their death; and their punishment will not be in vain.

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: Charles marks the phrase from their death with a dagger. The selected corpse-count clause remains difficult. The English is provisional and does not insert an unprinted negative, beyond counting, innumerable heaps, or an adopted retroverted Hebrew reading. The city is the city of my righteous ones, not silently his. The singular causative stir-up verb is not silently changed into they begin. Both the brother/son-family negatives and the final not-in-vain are retained.

source.text: በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ትፈትኅ፡ ሲኦል፡ አፉሃ፡ ወይሰጠሙ፡ ውስቴታ፡ ወኀጉሎሙ፡ ተፈጽማ፡ ሲኦል፡ ይውሕጦሙ፡ ለኃጥአን፡ እም*ቅድመ፡ ገጸ፡ ኅሩያን።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: In those days Sheol will open its mouth, and they will sink into it. Their destruction will be complete. Sheol will swallow the sinners from before the face of the chosen ones.

footnotes.text: Sheol retains the source name rather than identifying a later doctrinal account of hell. Its open mouth and swallowing are the text’s images. The sinking verb is not recast as a peaceful sleep. The selected text explicitly calls those swallowed sinners and distinguishes the chosen ones before whom they disappear.

source.text: ወ*ኮነ፡ እምድኅረዝ፡ ወርኢኩ፡ ካልአተ፡ ትዕይንተ፡ ሠረገላት፡ ወእንዘ፡ ይጽዐኑ፡ ሰብአ፡ ውስቴቶሙ፡ ወ*ይመጽኡ፡ ዲበ፡ ነፋሳት፡ እምምሥራቅ፡ ወእምምዕራብ፡ እስከ፡ መንገለ፡ ደቡብ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: After this I saw another troop of chariots, with people riding inside them. They were coming on the winds from the east and from the west, toward the south.

footnotes.text: The riding verb is supported by the primary lexicon’s explicit reference to this passage. The people are inside the chariots in the selected wording. Winds fits the printed directional journey; no named spirit or unprinted northern direction is added.

source.text: ወ*ተሰምዐ፡ ቃለ፡ ድምፀ፡ ሠረገላቲሆሙ፡ ወሶበ፡ ኮነ፡ ዘሁውከት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ እምሰማይ፡ አእመሩ፡ ወዐምደ፡ ምድር፡ ተሐውሰ፡ እመንበሩ፡ ወ*ተሰምዐ፡ እምአጽናፈ፡ ሰማይ፡ *እስከ፡ አጽናፈ፡ በአሐቱ፡ ዕለት።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: The sound of their chariots was heard. When this tumult arose, the holy ones in heaven became aware of it. The pillar of the earth shook from its base, and it was heard from one end of heaven to the other in a single day.

footnotes.text: The selected text says the holy ones became aware of the tumult from heaven. It has a singular pillar of the earth and its singular base, and it specifies a single day. Neither the singular nor the numeral is normalized to a familiar rendering.

source.text: ወ*ይወድቁ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ወ*ይሰግዱ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወ*ዝንቱ፡ ውእቱ፡ ተፍጻሜት፡ ካልእ፡ ምሳሌ።
source.note: Author collated complete selected-edition main text from actual full photographs and native400dpi crops. Printed stars, dagger, closing bracket and dots retained; raised apparatus references excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. No modern/later English translation or fresh manuscript inspection used.

translation.text: They will all fall down and worship the Lord of Spirits. This is the end of the second parable.

footnotes.text: The conclusion explicitly says second parable. The ordinal is retained; no extra parable or separate chapter-end speech is supplied.
